POST /v1/shop/wishlist/items/:productId.description: For a signed-in shopper (SS-Sign-In), else 403 sign_in_required; a guest's wishlist is kept in their browser and joined at sign-in (POST /v1/shop/wishlist/merge). Saving a saved product changes nothing. 404 not_found when the product is not active (or in a hidden category or brand); 422 validation_failed at /productId when the wishlist holds 200 products already.

SS-Sign-In.description: The shopper's Accounts sign-in (as the Accounts widgets give it).

POST /v1/shop/wishlist/merge.summary: Join a guest's wishlist to the shopper's
POST /v1/shop/wishlist/merge.description: For a signed-in shopper (SS-Sign-In), else 403 sign_in_required; a guest's wishlist is kept in their browser and joined at sign-in (POST /v1/shop/wishlist/merge). Products already saved keep their place; the active ones of the rest are added in the order given while there is room (200); others are skipped. More than 200 ids, or one that is not a product id, answer 422 validation_failed at /productIds.

DELETE /v1/shop/wishlist/items/:productI.summary: Remove a product from the wishlist
DELETE /v1/shop/wishlist/items/:productI.description: For a signed-in shopper (SS-Sign-In), else 403 sign_in_required; a guest's wishlist is kept in their browser and joined at sign-in (POST /v1/shop/wishlist/merge). Removing a product not saved changes nothing. Answers the wishlist.

GET /v1/shop/compare.description: On their comparable attributes, price, brand, grades, rating and image. ids names 1 to the compare setting maxProducts (2–4, default 4) products; repeats are dropped. Too many or none, or an id that is not a product id, answer 422 validation_failed at /ids.

ids.description: Comma-separated product ids (prd_…), in the order to show.

GET /v1/landings.description: Every matching landing page by id (at most 2,000; not paged), each with its address, its products in stock and whether search engines index it now.

category.description: Only landing pages of this category id.

brand.description: Only landing pages of this brand id.

grade.description: Only landing pages of this grade key.

q.description: Words found in the heading, the title or the category's or brand's name (any case).

POST /v1/landings.description: A category, brand and grade combination (at least one) with its own heading, title, description, introduction and FAQs; one landing page per combination. 422 validation_failed at /categoryId when none of categoryId, brandId and grade is given or the category does not exist, at /brandId or /grade (a key of your grades list) when it does not exist, or at a text that is too long; 409 conflict when another landing page has the same combination or when the website has 2,000. url comes from the landing_pages setting landingUrl; indexable auto is indexed while at least landingMinProducts of its products are in stock. Send an Idempotency-Key so a retried request makes one landing page.

PATCH /v1/landings/:id.description: Members left out keep their value; null (or '') clears categoryId, brandId or grade, but one of them must stay. 404 not_found; 422 validation_failed at /categoryId when none of categoryId, brandId and grade is given or the category does not exist, at /brandId or /grade (a key of your grades list) when it does not exist, or at a text that is too long; 409 conflict when another landing page has the same combination.

POST /v1/landings/:id/ai-copy.summary: Suggest a landing page's copy with AI
POST /v1/landings/:id/ai-copy.description: Your AI provider (Connections) writes the fields asked for from the page's category, brand and grade and up to 20 of its best-selling products, in the ai_copy settings' tone and language unless given. Nothing is saved. Needs AI copy and Landing pages on (403 feature_off). 422 validation_failed at /fields or /tone; 404 not_found; 503 ai_not_connected without an AI connection; 502 ai_failed when the provider fails or gives no usable text.

category.description: Only landing pages of this category id.

brand.description: Only landing pages of this brand id.

grade.description: Only landing pages of this grade key.

q.description: Words found in the heading, the title or the category's or brand's name (any case).

Nothing is saved. GET /v1/seo/listing.summary: The head of a listing page
GET /v1/seo/listing.description: Pass your listing page's query as it is. robots is index (the category's own noindex and nofollow aside) only for a category without other filters (and its pages) and for a landing page that is indexed now and matches the filters exactly; any other filter, a hidden brand or a category coming soon gives noindex, follow. With the seo setting pagedListings noindex, pages 2, 3 … are noindex, follow with the first page as canonical (index: each page its own canonical, ?page=n). Title and description follow the landing page, the category's SEO fields or the seo settings' patterns, titleTemplate and defaultDescription. An earlier category slug answers moved; 404 not_found for an unknown or hidden category.

category.description: The category: its id, slug (any case) or an earlier slug.

brand.description: A brand id or slug (several, comma-separated, count as a filter).

grade.description: A grade key (several, comma-separated, count as a filter).

page.description: The page number (1 when left out).

GET /v1/seo/attributes/:slug.description: :slug is the attribute's slug (any case) or id. Its own glossary SEO, else the landing_pages patterns attributeTitle and attributeDescription. canonical is the landing_pages setting attributeUrl with {slug}; without it the page is noindex, follow. 404 not_found for an unknown or inactive attribute.

GET /v1/seo/grades/:key.description: canonical is the landing_pages setting gradeUrl with {key}; without it the page is noindex, follow. 404 not_found when Grades and serials is off, or for an unknown grade or one not offered (active false).

GET /v1/seo/products/:ref.summary: A product page's meta tags and structured data
GET /v1/seo/products/:ref.description: :ref is the product's id or slug (any case). An earlier slug answers moved to the product; an archived product answers moved to its first category when the catalog setting retiredUrl is category. 404 not_found for an unknown product, a draft, an archived one otherwise, or one shoppers may not see (a hidden category or brand).

GET /v1/seo/categories/:ref.summary: A category page's meta tags and structured data
GET /v1/seo/categories/:ref.description: :ref is the category's id or slug (any case); an earlier slug answers moved. While it is coming soon, status is coming_soon, robots noindex, follow and its ItemList is empty. 404 not_found for an unknown or hidden category.

GET /v1/seo/sitemap.xml.description: Answers application/xml, not JSON: a urlset (with the image extension) of the categories shoppers see, the indexable landing and glossary pages (Landing pages) and the active products shoppers may see with up to 10 images each, leaving out pages marked noindex, with lastmod. Above the seo setting sitemapSize addresses (10,000 by default) it is a sitemapindex instead, whose files are the seo setting sitemapUrl with ?file=categories, ?file=landings, ?file=products-1 … (serve each from GET /v1/seo/sitemaps/:file).

GET /v1/seo/sitemaps/:file.summary: One file of the sitemap index
GET /v1/seo/sitemaps/:file.description: :file is categories, landings or products-<n> (.xml may follow). Answers application/xml, not JSON: a urlset of that part (products-<n>: the n-th sitemapSize products by id). 404 not_found for a file the index does not have (an empty part has none).

GET /v1/feeds/products.xml.description: Answers application/xml, not JSON: an RSS 2.0 feed with the g: namespace, one item per active variant priced above 0 of every active product shoppers may see (at most 100,000), with g:id, item_group_id, title, description, link, image_link, availability, price, sale_price, condition, brand, gtin, mpn, identifier_exists, product_type, google_product_category, custom_label_0 and shipping (empty fields left out). Shaped by the feeds settings: items (with_images or all), includeOutOfStock, itemTitle, itemDescription, skuAs, identifierExists, gradedCondition, itemId, googleCategory and gradeLabel; shipping from Delivery zones. The cost is never in it.

GET /v1/feeds/products.csv.description: Answers text/csv, not JSON: a header line, then one line per active variant priced above 0 of every active product shoppers may see (at most 100,000), with the columns id, title, description, availability, condition, price (the price the shopper pays), link, image_link, brand, item_group_id, google_product_category and custom_label_0 (RFC 4180, CRLF line ends). The same feeds settings as products.xml.

GET /v1/llms.txt.description: Answers text/plain (Markdown), not JSON: the business name, the llms_txt setting description, the categories shoppers see in tree order (up to 200), the best-selling products (the llms_txt setting products, up to 200, with price and summary) and, unless the setting policies is off, the shop's policies as text.

GET /v1/llms-full.txt.description: Answers text/plain (Markdown), not JSON: every active product in stock shoppers may see (up to 50,000) with its price range, by category, with the grades of each category. 404 not_found while the llms_txt setting full is off.

GET /v1/shop/policies.description: For the visitor (browser token). The checkout settings policyShipping, policyReturns, policyPrivacy, policyTerms and policyWarranty, with {returnDays}, {warrantyDays}, {warrantyMonths}, {business}, {email}, {phone}, {address} (business.json), {deliveryFee} and {freeDeliveryOver} (Delivery zones, as money) filled in (also written with double braces); other text in braces stays.

GET /v1/policies.description: For your own policy pages (server token). The checkout settings policyShipping, policyReturns, policyPrivacy, policyTerms and policyWarranty, with {returnDays}, {warrantyDays}, {warrantyMonths}, {business}, {email}, {phone}, {address} (business.json), {deliveryFee} and {freeDeliveryOver} (Delivery zones, as money) filled in (also written with double braces); other text in braces stays.

POST /v1/import/:collection.description: collection is one of size_charts, categories, brands, attributes, landings, products, serials, deals, bundles, customers, orders, loyalty, reviews, returns, alerts, wishlists; import them in that order (records must name records of an earlier step), then call finish. The body is application/x-ndjson (Content-Type), not JSON: one record per line, at most 1,000 records or 4 MB per call. Records are Ecommerce's stored shapes, every one with optional createdAt and updatedAt: size_charts { id (szc_), name, unit, columns, rows, fitAdvice, notes, active }; categories { id (cat_), slug, name, parentId, description, seo, image, sort, status, icon, content, faqs, sizeChartId, requiresSerial, previousSlugs }; brands { id (brd_), slug, name, description, logo, status, categoryIds, seo, sizeChartId }; attributes { id (att_), name, type, choices, unit, slug, categoryIds, on, multiple, visibility, card, active, seo … }; landings { id (lnd_), categoryId, brandId, grade, h1, title, description, intro, faqs, indexable }; products { id (prd_), slug, name, kind, status, … variants (var_ ids), media, sold, rating, publishedAt, previousSlugs } (a product without a variant is stored as a draft); serials { id (ser_), productId, variantId, serial, status, orderId, lineId, locationId }; deals (deal_) and bundles (bnd_) with their use count used; customers { id (cus_), userId, name, email, phone, city, blocked … }; orders { id (ord_), number, customer, address, delivery, lines, totals, promotions, payment, payments, refunds, status, history, shipment … } (money in minor units, adding up as checkout adds it); loyalty { customerId, userId, lots, history … }; reviews (rev_); returns (ret_); alerts (alr_); wishlists { userId, productIds }. Each record is found by its key: id (<prefix>_<10 to 64 of 0-9a-z>), customerId for loyalty, userId for wishlists. Each record passes Ecommerce's own check in import mode: given ids, numbers, past times and histories are kept; fields the record type does not have and values the shop derives (a category's path, a product's price or stockState …) are refused by name, as is text over a limit (never cut); slugs, SKUs, variant ids, serial numbers and landing combinations another record holds are refused. A checked record replaces the stored one (createdAt kept when it has none), so a re-run changes nothing. Nothing is sent: no message, event, alert, activity copy or IndexNow call, and no stock is held. Server token only. 404 not_found for another collection; 415 unsupported_media_type without NDJSON; 413 payload_too_large.

dryRun.description: Check and count only; nothing is written.

POST /v1/import/:collection/prune.summary: Remove imported records the source no longer has
POST /v1/import/:collection/prune.description: collection as for importing. Removes the records an import wrote whose key lies after after and up to through (open ends when left out; keys compared as UTF-8 bytes) and is not in keep, at most 1,000 per call (more: call again). Records made in the shop itself are never removed. Send application/json: 415 unsupported_media_type otherwise; 422 validation_failed for a malformed keep, after or through; 413 payload_too_large above 1,000 keys. 404 not_found for another collection.

dryRun.description: Answer what would go; nothing is removed.

keep.description: The source's keys in this range (ids; customerId for loyalty, userId for wishlists), sorted.

after.description: The range starts after this key.

through.description: The range ends with this key.

POST /v1/import/finish.summary: Finish an import: derive what the shop keeps
POST /v1/import/finish.description: Run after the imports (and again whenever more is imported): it derives every category's path from the parents, products' price, price range, stock state and grades, customers' order and RTO counts and last order, loyalty balances and lifetime points, products' sold count (from delivered order lines) and rating (from approved reviews) where their order lines or reviews were imported too (otherwise the imported numbers stay), serials sold through order lines, and the order-number counters. It writes only what differs, so a second run changes nothing.

GET /v1/import/status.summary: What is stored, for ss-import verify
GET /v1/import/status.description: Records per collection, those an import wrote, and the sums ss-import verify compares.
